data.name: Intro
data.value: This guide lists the values to enter in the Microsoft Intune admin center for build {0}. It only describes settings. It does not show that anything was uploaded, assigned or installed.

data.name: MixWarningText
data.value: Use the package file {0} and the detection script {1} of this build ({2}) only together. If you combine the .intunewin file of one version with the detection script of another build, Intune checks for the wrong state.

data.name: ValRestartByCodes
data.value: Determine behavior based on return codes

data.name: NoteRestart
data.value: The package never forces a restart. A restart is only requested through the return codes in section 6.

data.name: NoteProcessesToClose
data.value: The package asks the user to close these programs. It does not end them by force.

data.name: NotePlaceholder
data.value: Placeholder: this value has not been decided yet. Check it against your environment before you rely on it.

data.name: NoteReturnCodes
data.value: Enter every code of this table. Intune treats codes that are not listed as failures.

data.name: NoteReturn1641
data.value: Code 1641 means that the installer already restarted the device. It is listed as hard reboot and never as a quiet success.

data.name: FldRun32
data.value: Run script as 32-bit process on 64-bit clients

data.name: FldSignatureCheck
data.value: Enforce script signature check and run script silently

data.name: NoteSignature
data.value: The script is not signed, so the signature check must stay off. Intune would not accept an unsigned script with the check on.

data.name: RuleMsi
data.value: The product code {0} is installed (32-bit or 64-bit registry view) with version {1} or higher.

data.name: RuleFile
data.value: The file {0} exists and has file version {1} or higher.

data.name: NoteContract
data.value: Intune treats the app as detected when the script ends with exit code 0 and writes text to standard output. The script reads the real state of the device and uses no files of the package.

data.name: AssignPilot
data.value: Assign the app to a pilot group first and check the result on test devices before a wider rollout. This tool assigns nothing and has no access to your tenant.

data.name: AssignRequired
data.value: Required: Intune installs the app on the devices or for the users of the group.

data.name: AssignAvailable
data.value: Available for enrolled devices: users decide themselves and install the app from the Company Portal.

data.name: DepNone
data.value: This package defines none. Add them in Intune only if you need them.

data.name: TroubleStep1
data.value: Open the deployment log and read the last entries first.

data.name: TroubleStep2
data.value: For an MSI package, open the MSI log and search for the text "return value 3".

data.name: TroubleStep3
data.value: Check the Intune Management Extension logs for the exit code that Intune received.

data.name: TroubleStep4
data.value: Run the detection script in a 64-bit Windows PowerShell with administrator rights. Exit code 0 with output means detected.

data.name: NoteVendorLogs
data.value: Vendor installers can write more logs to their own paths. Check the vendor documentation.

data.name: Footer
data.value: Generated by Intune Package Builder for build {0}. The values on this page belong to this build only.
